deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, equations or calculations. It is a heavily corrected prose draft of the section 'Paukenhöhle' (tympanic cavity) of Riemann's posthumous fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres', published by Henle in 1866/67 and included in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke. The marginal 'p. 10' and 'p. 18' are probably page references to a fair copy or to a cited source.

Content, in order:

(a) The page opens by finishing a sentence from the preceding page: '...zu einer genügenden Lösung der Aufgabe erforderlich ist.'

(b) Heading 'Paukenhöhle'. It has long been recognised that the middle-ear apparatus exists to transmit the air pressure (on the eardrum) to the water of the labyrinth. The guiding question is: by what means is this achieved under all circumstances with the precision and fineness that experience of the ear's performance demands? This question must be kept in view throughout the study of the tympanic apparatus. This is an application of the programme on the previous page: infer the structure from the ear's performance, then derive the conditions the parts must satisfy.

(c) Mechanical description. The apparatus transmits the force of the air on the eardrum to the oval window. It consists of the three ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes). They are joined by articulations in such a way that, during operation, they do not change their relative position and move as one rigid body. That motion is a rotation about an axis whose two ends are fixed:
- One end is the short process of the incus, articulated to a projection on the posterior wall of the tympanic cavity.
- The other end is the long (anterior) process of the malleus, lodged at the fissura petrotympanica (Glaserian fissure). It can change position only within narrow limits.

In modern terms: a rigid lever with one degree of freedom, a rotation angle phi about a fixed axis. Every point moves with displacement equal to phi times its distance from the axis.

(d) Kinematics. When the manubrium (handle of the malleus) is drawn inward, the stapes footplate is pressed against the membrane of the oval window. The pressure in the labyrinth fluid then rises and is relieved again (apparently via the round window; this reading is uncertain).

(e) Requirement. If the apparatus is to serve accurate hearing, the stapes footplate must always act on the labyrinth fluid in exactly the same way. Riemann starts a list of necessary conditions:
1) The pressure exerted by the footplate, and the effect of the motion, must be invariable (a fixed, unchanging relation; heavily struck through).
2) The transmission must not be disturbed by membranes... (the sentence breaks off).

The implicit modern content, which is mine and not on the page, is that the transmission should be a fixed, single-valued, time-invariant map from eardrum force to footplate pressure. This is the idea that the published 'Mechanik des Ohres' develops as the demand for distortion-free transmission of small pressure changes.
errors: The anatomical description (ossicular chain rotating as one rigid body about an axis through the short incus process and the anterior malleus process) is the standard 19th-century view, later refined by Helmholtz (1868). Treating the chain as perfectly rigid is an idealisation; the malleus-incus joint is not rigid for large or static displacements, as Helmholtz's 'Sperrzähne' analysis showed.
The final conditions 1) and 2) are left incomplete and heavily cancelled, so the intended list cannot be fully recovered.

results.what: Statement that the middle ear's task is to transmit air pressure on the eardrum to the labyrinth fluid, with the precision demanded by auditory performance as the guiding question
results.usually_credited_to: Long-standing physiological view (e.g., J. Müller, Weber brothers); quantitative theory Helmholtz 1868

results.what: Ossicular chain moving as one rigid body rotating about a fixed axis from the short incus process (posterior wall) to the anterior malleus process (Glaserian fissure)
results.modern_name: Ossicular axis of rotation (lever model of the ossicles)
results.usually_credited_to: Anatomists before 1860 (axis description); mechanical analysis Helmholtz 1868

results.what: Requirement that the stapes footplate always act on the labyrinth fluid in an identical, invariable way (fidelity condition)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the known, published 'Mechanik des Ohres' (Gesammelte Werke). The content is qualitative physiological mechanics with no mathematics, and it matches the published text and the standard view of the time.

checkable.sympy: phi, r1, r2 = symbols('phi r1 r2', positive=True); simplify((phi*r2)/(phi*r1) - r2/r1) == 0
checkable.asserts: For a rigid body rotating by small angle phi about a fixed axis, displacements of two points are in the fixed ratio of their distances from the axis (the implicit lever model). This is my addition, not written on the page.

transcription_corrections: The opening line is the end of a sentence carried over from the previous page: '| zu einer genügenden Lösung der Aufgabe erforderlich ist.'

The guiding-question sentence should read roughly: 'Durch welche Mittel diese Aufgabe unter allen Umständen mit einer so grossen / solchen Genauigkeit und Feinheit gelöst wird, welche den Erfahrungen über die Leistungen des Ohrs entspricht, dieses ist die Frage, welche wir ... bei der Betrachtung des Paukenapparats fortwährend festhalten und zu beantworten suchen müssen.'
'Der Apparat, welcher den von der Luft auf das Trommelfell ausgeübten Druck auf das ovale Fenster überträgt': 'Trommel' replaces cancelled 'Pauken'.
'deren eines Ende, der kurze Fortsatz des Ambos' is correct; the cancelled word before it is probably 'Stützpunkt / Unterstützungspunkt'.
'der lange Fortsatz des Hammers an der fissura petrotympanica steckt': the reading of 'fissura petrotympanica' looks right from the image (= Glaserian fissure).

The cancelled/interlined phrase after 'der Druck im Labyrinthwasser gesteigert und' seems to refer to equalisation through the round window ('durch das runde Fenster ... ausgeglichen'); the reading is uncertain.
'Soll der Apparat dem genauen Hören entsprechend sein' is a plausible reading of the line beginning 'Soll der Apparat ...'.
